While **passato prossimo** describes a completed action, **imperfetto** describes habitual, ongoing, or descriptive actions in the past — "used to" or "was ...ing" in English.

Regular endings: **-are → -avo, -avi, -ava, -avamo, -avate, -avano**; **-ere/-ire → -evo/-ivo, -evi/-ivi, -eva/-iva, -evamo/-ivamo, -evate/-ivate, -evano/-ivano**. **Essere** is irregular: **ero, eri, era, eravamo, eravate, erano**.

exercises.prompt: Da bambino, io ___ sempre fuori. (giocare — As a child, I always used to play outside.)
Da giovane, lei ___ molto timida. (essere — When she was young, she used to be very shy.)
Translate: "We used to live in Rome." (abitare — to live)
